package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://pymafka.evil.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are accessed and exfiltrated to an external server controlled by the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials.
The package initiates outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://pymafka.evil.com/upload during setup.py execution.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and sends data to an external domain
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations where setup.py accesses sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and initiates outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://pymafka.evil.com/upload. Flag any package containing code in setup.py that reads these files and sends their contents to external domains.
